newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends lower, market digesting rate news.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends lower, market digesting rate news.

text.p: Romania's leu closed on Monday weaker at 6,700/750 to the dollar from 6,450/500 in early trading on a market hit by dollar shortages and digesting news that the central bank would make key rates more flexible.

On Monday central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu said the Lombard rate, now at an annual 90 percent, would start floating this week in line with the one-week rate on its auctioned refinancing credits.
Isarescu said the Lombard would move upward to some 144 percent on Friday if the one-week rate stays at last week's level of 90 percent.
"This move proves that the BNR is determined to implement market mechanisms. Rates will be much closer to market reality, and will much better reflect demand and supply," said a trader.
Operators said the market had already anticipated an increase in the Lombard rate after the one-week rate jumped to 90 percent from 81 percent last week.
Some traders said the recent tightening in the BNR monetary policies might give the leu some support but they said an appreciation was unlikely.
"The leu might stay flat for a while but in the longer term it is poised to slide further due to inflationary fears and as the market remains short of hard currency," said one trader.
Leu-dollar retail prices hovered at 6,350/650 with traders saying new lows were expected in the coming days.
The money market remained illiquid and cash-hungry with overnight funds at about 87-88 percent.
